Iran’s Central Bank said the consumer price index reached 77.2% and inflation in daily and general needs rose 113.8% since last May.

A private economic think tank in Iran described the figures as “an unprecedented rate since World War II.”

Activist Sepide Qoliyan was recently released from prison and speaks of a woman named Azar, who was imprisoned for merely using a messaging app sticker of Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu.

"I don’t think there’s any country in the world that would accuse someone of 'collaborating with Israel' and throw them into solitary confinement over a sticker, but here it’s routine. The more our longing for freedom grows, the more the repression grows..."

Anti-regime protests continue in Iran for a second day, sparked by the rapidly devaluing rial.

A brave protest of one: a protester sits with his jacket pulled over his head—presumably to protect his identity—as he faces security forces.
